scope: Editorial prototype. Connections express proximity/influence, not a definitive genealogical claim. Emergence years approximate and frequently debated.

genres.name: Hypnagogic pop
genres.description: Degraded pop-memory, warped nostalgia and DIY recordings that blurred the line between familiar media and dream.

genres.name: Chillwave
genres.description: Hazy synthesizers, softened beats and nostalgic pop textures circulated through late-2000s music blogs.

genres.name: Vaporwave
genres.description: An internet-born style of slowed samples, imagined corporate spaces and unsettling nostalgia for familiar commercial sound.

genres.name: Eccojams
genres.description: Short pop fragments looped, slowed and transformed into hypnotic repetition; an influential precursor to vaporwave.

genres.name: Mallsoft
genres.description: Reverberant retail ambience: distant muzak, public-space field recordings and the sound of an empty shopping centre.

genres.name: Future funk
genres.description: Sample-driven disco and city-pop edits with brighter momentum and dance rhythms than much early vaporwave.

genres.name: Signalwave
genres.description: Weather broadcasts, station idents and other transmissions edited into the sound of unreliable media memory.

genres.name: Slushwave
genres.description: Slow-moving ambient vaporwave: long-form, densely reverberant loops designed for immersion.

genres.name: Hardvapour
genres.description: An abrasive response to vaporwave, bringing gabber, hardcore and industrial intensity into its digital mythology.

genres.name: Barber beats
genres.description: A later vaporwave-adjacent style centred on looped instrumental groove, downtempo and lounge samples.

genres.name: Dreampunk
genres.description: Cinematic ambient atmospheres and imagined nocturnal futures, often connected to vaporwave communities.

genres.name: Seapunk
genres.description: A short-lived Tumblr-era scene joining aqueous cyber-aesthetics with eclectic electronic dance and pop.

genres.name: Witch house
genres.description: Heavily processed voices, slow tempos, industrial shadows and occult-coded internet imagery.

genres.name: Electropop
genres.description: Pop built around electronic production and synthesis; a broad pre-existing language later exaggerated by online scenes.

genres.name: Chiptune
genres.description: Music built from videogame sound-chip techniques, deeply influential in internet-era DIY electronic production.

genres.name: Bitpop
genres.description: Pop melodies fused with videogame timbres, digital noise and chip-inspired synthesis.

genres.name: Bubblegum bass
genres.description: Hyperreal, glossy, plastic-sounding pop associated with the PC Music movement and related producers.

genres.name: Nightcore
genres.description: Sped-up and pitched-up transformations of existing tracks, amplified by video and fan-upload cultures.

genres.name: Happy hardcore
genres.description: Euphoric high-speed rave music with bright melodies; a historical influence on some accelerated internet pop.

genres.name: Hyperpop
genres.description: A contested umbrella for maximalist and digitally manipulated pop, spanning different scenes and generations.

genres.name: Digicore
genres.description: A Discord- and SoundCloud-linked community mixing pop distortion, trap, pitch processing and DIY collaboration.

genres.name: Dariacore
genres.description: Breakneck, meme-literate sample collage associated with Jane Remover’s leroy project and online remix culture.

genres.name: Scenecore
genres.description: A loose internet scene revisiting MySpace-era electronic emo and scene aesthetics through contemporary production.

genres.name: Glitch pop
genres.description: Pop songwriting incorporating edits, digital stutters and fragmented audio as prominent musical material.

genres.name: Deconstructed club
genres.description: Club-derived music that fractures rhythmic expectations, foregrounding sound design and discontinuous energy.

genres.name: Post-club
genres.description: A loose term for club-informed experiments that depart from conventional dance-floor structures.

genres.name: Weightless grime
genres.description: Sparse, suspended instrumental grime often replacing drum impact with atmosphere and negative space.

genres.name: Future grime
genres.description: An informal tag for abstract, synthesizer-forward extensions of instrumental grime.

genres.name: Hard drum
genres.description: Percussion-forward UK club experimentation informed by multiple rhythmic traditions and dance scenes.

genres.name: Wonky
genres.description: Lopsided electronic rhythms, dislocated synth harmonies and off-centre beat programming.

genres.name: Glitch
genres.description: Clicks, errors and digital artifacts repurposed as musical material, predating many web-born microgenres.

genres.name: Breakcore
genres.description: Breakbeat acceleration, extreme edits and dense sample collisions; older than its later online revivals.

genres.name: Jungle revival
genres.description: New waves of jungle and breakbeat production circulated through online scenes, informed by 1990s dance history.

genres.name: Cloud rap
genres.description: Hazy pads, submerged drums and atmospheric production associated with early internet rap networks.

genres.name: SoundCloud rap
genres.description: A broad platform-linked rap wave spanning DIY recording, distorted mixes, emo influences and regional styles.

genres.name: Emo rap
genres.description: Rap integrated with confessional emo, rock guitar and melodic writing, accelerated by online communities.

genres.name: Plugg
genres.description: Bright synth loops, buoyant melodies and minimal trap drums associated with independent producer networks.

genres.name: Pluggnb
genres.description: Plugg rhythms filtered through lush R&B chords, melodic vocal runs and atmospheric synth textures.

genres.name: Rage
genres.description: High-impact trap with saturated synthetic leads and emphatic, high-energy rhythmic arrangements.

genres.name: Sigilkore
genres.description: Occult-coded online rap centred on chopped mixing, bitcrushing, pitch manipulation and abrasive digital effects.

genres.name: HexD
genres.description: Aggressively bitcrushed, pitch-shifted rap and trance-associated mixing aesthetic from internet communities.

genres.name: Jerk revival
genres.description: Off-kilter, quick-moving internet rap reworking the earlier jerk sound with new synth and low-end approaches.

genres.name: Krushclub
genres.description: Club-energy rap and electronic hybrids with heavily processed vocal and bass sounds.

genres.name: Phonk
genres.description: Memphis-rap-derived sample textures and distorted underground hip-hop practices, later taking varied forms online.

genres.name: Drift phonk
genres.description: A later electronically intensified phonk branch associated with cowbells, heavy bass and short-form video.

genres.name: Jersey club
genres.description: Newark-rooted club music known for triplet kick patterns, chops and a specific regional dance tradition.

genres.name: Baltimore club
genres.description: Baltimore dance music built from chopped breaks, repeated vocal hooks and hard physical club rhythms.

genres.name: Ballroom beats
genres.description: Sounds shaped by Black and Latin queer ballroom culture; a living social tradition, not merely a production preset.

genres.name: Footwork
genres.description: Fast, syncopated Chicago music inseparable from its footwork dancing communities.

genres.name: Juke
genres.description: Chicago club sound whose rapid patterns and local history helped shape footwork.

genres.name: UK funky
genres.description: London-rooted house-related sound with syncopated percussion and Caribbean and African dance influences.

genres.name: Gqom
genres.description: Durban-rooted, skeletal and percussive club music with distinctive rhythmic space and local cultural origins.

genres.name: Neo-perreo
genres.description: Internet-connected experimental reggaeton and perreo, pushing synthetic textures and alternative club aesthetics.

genres.name: Baile funk
genres.description: Brazilian funk culture rooted in Rio de Janeiro; connected to evolving local scenes and production lineages.

genres.name: Funk mandelão
genres.description: A São Paulo-linked baile funk form featuring spare, hard-edged electronic percussion and bass.
